findings.rationale: BMI has a lower tail that is impossible for real BMI (1st percentile about 0.09, sd inflated to 10 vs a federation median of 6.6), consistent with zeros used as a sentinel for missing values. PhysHlth has an inflated upper tail (mean 12 vs median 4.5, 99th percentile about 73 vs a median of 30), consistent with a missing-value sentinel code. Both patterns are present already in round 1, so the artefact starts at the beginning. Noise-adjusted z-scores are far beyond the screen threshold.

Same signature as AZ. BMI 1st percentile is negative (about -0.14) with sd of 11 vs a median of 6.6, consistent with a 0 sentinel. PhysHlth 99th percentile is about 74 with mean 10.8, consistent with a missing-value sentinel in the upper tail. Already present in round 1.

Same signature as AZ and KS. BMI 1st percentile near zero (about 0.48 at round 20, -0.16 at round 1) with inflated sd, and PhysHlth 99th percentile about 68-74 with mean about 12, consistent with sentinel codes replacing missing values. Present from round 1.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and subgroup outcomes for Sex, AgeGroup and Income (about 20 of 20 epsilon used, with confirmations). The update-norm and cosine screens show no poisoning, free-rider or explanation-instability pattern beyond weak min-cos values (AZ z=-3.3, MT z=-3.1) that are not corroborated. Client performance shows no consistent label-noise or prevalence-shift signature; GU's CITL z=-3.3 is on a small client (n=237) and is not corroborated. Subgroup outliers (CT AgeGroup 1, AK AgeGroup 10, ME AgeGroup 5, MI AgeGroup 3, NH Income 2, NC/CO/AK/GU Sex) are small-group, noise-dominated; the CT follow-up with more epsilon gave per-group values clipped to 0 or 1, which indicates noise rather than a real effect. The drift screen flagged no client, and the VI follow-up was too noisy to interpret. The clear finding is a missing-value sentinel artefact in BMI and PhysHlth on AZ, KS and MT, present from round 1. Confidence in the other clients being clean is moderate, given the budget limits and noise on small clients.
